definition: The training objective in which a language model learns to predict the most likely next token given the preceding sequence of tokens.
details: This deceptively simple objective, applied at massive scale, is the core mechanism by which LLMs learn grammar, facts, reasoning patterns, and style from raw text.

explainer.lead: Next-token prediction is the training objective in which a language model learns to predict the most likely next token given the preceding sequence. It matters because this simple objective, applied at massive scale, is the core mechanism by which large language models learn grammar, facts, reasoning patterns, and style from raw text.

tiers.eli5: The model plays a guessing game, over and over, trying to predict the next word in a sentence, and by doing that millions of times it learns how language and facts fit together.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train language models by repeatedly predicting the next token over raw text at scale, with no explicit labels for grammar or facts; a pitfall is expecting reasoning to be taught directly rather than emerging from this objective.
tiers.paperLevel: Next-token prediction is the training objective in which a language model learns to predict the most likely token given the preceding sequence of tokens; applied at massive scale, it is the core mechanism by which LLMs learn grammar, facts, reasoning patterns, and style from raw text.

explainer.example: Trained on raw text by predicting each next token from its predecessors, a model acquires grammar and factual patterns without being given explicit rules.
